data.$description: Charting semantics — V7 RULED+CONFIRMED Dave 2026-07-16 (render sheet reviews/DATAVIZ-SERIES-RENDERS-2026-07-16.html REV 3; holding pen tokens/_proposals/dataviz-ranges.proposals.json). series = range/default: mode-stable candidate C, SAME value both modes (dv-014 categorisation-consistency held ACROSS the theme switch; conscious divergence from col26-017 palette-halves, receipted). series-high-contrast = range/high-contrast: candidate A, bound per chart via data-contrast/data-range (token rebind, no chart forks). delta = D2 convention-forward with BOTH pairs value-split for the vibrating-boundaries rule (astigmatism a11y; legs value-ratio<1.25 + hue-sep>=135 + sat>=0.5); scoped col26-012 override recorded in guidelines/data-visualisation.md — delta indicators only, NEVER series fills; sign+arrow mandatory (dv-011). warning = graphic-grade 3:1 in light (col26-018), luminous on dark.

axis.$description: DV-D07 (RULED Dave 2026-07-23, ledger _proforma/_DATAVIZ-DECISIONS.md): chart chrome role — axis text, tick numerals and axis-adjacent ink. TWO-CHANNEL (extends ADR-0009 physics beyond states, ADR-0010 slot posture): per-mode COLOUR snapped to the neutral ramp + a declared ALPHA flex slot, default 1.0. Only a theme pulling the alpha lever populates <1; where alpha<1, dv-016/DV-D03 contrast computes from the COMPOSITE (colour × alpha × ground), never the stored hex. Closes worker-D's receipted quiet-ink gap (post-R-D16 homeless greys). Starting values = the Q6 decision sheet (reviews/DATA-AXIS-GRID-2026-07-23-v1.html), re-diallable there. data/target deferred to chart-revisit Q4.

alpha.$note: declared flex slot (ADR-0010) — unitless, default 1.0 (full). Dave verbatim (DV-D07): 'store a null or 100% value plus the colour; going forward I need max flexibility so creating new themes has many levels to pull on.'

grid.$description: DV-D07 (RULED Dave 2026-07-23): chart chrome role — gridlines. Same two-channel shape as data/axis. Gridlines are decorative chrome (WCAG 1.4.11-exempt; dv-016 gridline contrast is ADVISORY by design — quiet is the point).

control.$description: ds-018 A2 (RULED Dave 2026-07-27, ledger _DS-IMPROVEMENTS.md ds-018): dataviz-tier CONTROL chrome — the legend's own interactive furniture, sibling of data/axis and data/grid. Minted because the chart scopes were reading FORM-tier tokens (--border-disabled, --text-disabled) that are declared on ten .cn-* form scopes and ZERO chart scopes, so both resolved to nothing and border-color fell to currentColor = ink: the dead control rendered 13.3x the contrast of the live one. CALL B (RULED B2) is label-led — the disabled BORDER returns to --line (enabled-resting) because the border channel is structurally unable to carry a recessive step (enabled resting is already 1.31:1, the perceptible floor), so the LABEL carries the whole distinction. That cost is RULED, not a defect to fix later.

label-disabled.$description: Recessive label step for a disabled dataviz control (the legend Reset). WCAG 1.4.3-EXEMPT (inactive component) so B-D5's AA clamp does not bind; the governing constraint is B-D4 — Dave: 'it doesn't have to be accessible but invisible for normal sighted people isn't acceptable.'

color.$note: VALUE = REUSE, NOT A NEW DERIVATION. This is B-D4's SETTLED pair (#9D9D9D light / #808080 dark) adopted verbatim for the dataviz tier. Dave 2026-07-27, on the efficiency question: 'just do it' — taken against an explicit statement that the alternative was a fresh value judgement, and that a token value is a one-line reversible edit rather than architecture. ⚠ CAVEAT RECORDED AT MINT, NOT DISCOVERED LATER: B-D4 dialled this pair against the DISABLED FILL #E1E1E1; here it sits on the CHART GROUND (the legend row has no background, Chart-bar.reference.html:203), so the same hex reads at a different ratio than the one that was judged. Re-dial on sight is expected and cheap. ⚠ Also corrects the record: B-D4 does NOT disagree with canon — its prose says '#808080 both modes' but its own Values-SETTLED block gives the light/dark pair that canon.css:351/:648 and this file both implement. The 'collision' carried in GOOD-MORNING/_LIVE-STATE was a misreading of the prose against half the ruling.

target.$description: DV-D07-pattern mint, enacted with menu pick 7 (threshold/target line — Dave ruled the menu IN, 2026-07-23 evening). Reference/target line ink, TWO-CHANNEL like data/axis + data/grid. VALUES PROPOSED BY AGENT (derivation governance — Dave re-dials): stronger than axis chrome (target is a read, not chrome), distinct from series hues; the DASH pattern is the non-colour channel. Light neutral/5, dark neutral/10.

text.$description: Type drawn ON a series fill, not on the page — the stacked bar's alpha keys (A/B/C) are the first consumer. MINTED 2026-07-27 by Dave's ruling, ds-014 call (b): the keys had been declaring var(--page), which renders white today only because of where the neutral ramp sits — a coincidence, not an intent, and it would resolve dark and vanish into the fill on a dark-page theme. Modelled on rag/text/on-dark (pinned white in BOTH modes), which is the proven shape for type on a chromatic ground. DELIBERATELY has no alpha channel, unlike its data/axis + data/grid + data/target siblings: DV-D07 requires contrast to compute from the composite (colour × alpha × ground), so an alpha slot here would be a route to a key that passes on the hex and fails on screen — the ds-013 shape. Full opacity is the contract.

digital-black.$name: digital black (Dave 2026-07-18: "it can be called digital black or something, that's probably how I'll remember it")
digital-black.$note: derived (no primitive alias) — the DIGITAL SUBSTITUTE for the brand black #000000 (color/black). ⚠️ CONDITIONAL, not a free second black: use ONLY where light/reverse text sits ON the dark ground. Pure black remains brand-canon and stays correct for borders, marks, rules and any surface carrying no reverse text. RATIONALE: #000 maximises the luminance step against white (21:1), which drives halation — the bright field blooming across the edge, read as text that 'dances'. #1A1A1A cuts that step ~17% to 17.4:1 and settles the text without reducing legibility. The NAME deliberately favours recall over precision (Dave's call, he is the one who must remember it) — it does NOT encode the condition, so the condition lives here and must travel with it. | ADR-0014: seated on color/neutral/4 (value-identical #1A1A1A). Under a warm theme the digital-black substrate follows the theme ramp (SC dark page = warm/4).
digital-black.$condition: light or reverse text sits on this ground
digital-black.$rule: reduce the extremity of the edge — the NEUTRAL-ground lever. Its coloured-ground twin is the saturation ceiling (≤0.72). Both reduce edge extremity; neither adds contrast, which makes halation worse.
digital-black.$provenance: in production use since ~2026-07-04 via _PROFORMA-RULES.md rule 1 (Apollo mono primary), but until 2026-07-18 it existed ONLY as prose — no token, no gate, rationale unrecorded. Promoted on Dave's ruling 2026-07-18. Holding-pen record: tokens/_proposals/neutral-blacks.proposals.json
